name: Web Share
plain: Opens the phone's native share sheet with text, a link or files.
meaning: The person picks the target app. The site does not learn which one.

access.iframe: Same as top level; cross-origin iframes need a permissions policy where listed

data.metric: Opens the phone's native share sheet with text, a link or files.

fields.name: files
fields.range: platform limit; images, video, audio, pdf, text

limits.headline: Can open your phone's share sheet with a link, text or files, only after a tap
limits.user_action: You tap a Share button on the page
can: Open the share sheet with text, a link or files
Let you pick the app to send to
Share one item at a time
cannot: Open the share sheet without a tap
Share anything you did not offer
Work in Firefox on most computers yet
limits.differs: Chrome, Edge, Safari and phone browsers support it. Firefox support is limited.

story.what_it_is: A page can open your phone's normal share sheet with a link, text or file.

marketing.name: Web Share API
marketing.pitch: Lets a site hand off a link, text or file to the share sheet, so you can send it with any app on your device.

story.for_you: You tap a Share button, and your device's own share menu appears. You pick an app or a person. Nothing is shared until you choose.
story.for_makers: Makers skip building buttons for each network, which saves work and clutters less. Share events bring new visitors. It must start from a tap, so it cannot fire by itself.

use_cases.example: A news article has one Share button that opens the share sheet for any chat or social app.
A browser game shares your high score with a friend through your messages app.
A store shares a product link with a friend for a gift idea.
A music site shares a track to your story or chat.
A travel site shares a trip plan with a travel partner.
A web photo tool shares an edited picture through the share sheet.
A social site shares a post link to another app.
A document site shares a view link with a coworker in one tap.
